description: Client file portal for firms that use Vibe Files: staff share files with clients from Vibe Files, and clients sign in to download them and send documents back into Vibe Files' Intake.
_doc: In-tree manifest for KisaesDevLab/Vibe-Portal (github.com/KisaesDevLab/Vibe-Portal). SLUG: `vibe-files-portal`, not `vibe-portal`. The appliance already uses `vibe-portal` as the broker key of its own landing-page sign-in gate (lib/identity.sh portal-gate, console/identity.js PORTAL_LOCK), so the app takes a distinct slug; the image is still ghcr.io/kisaesdevlab/vibe-portal. ONE container from one GHCR image: the Express API on :3101 serves the built client portal, the staff page (/staff) and /health, and applies its own migrations at boot. Shared Postgres only; no Redis. /data/portal holds the encrypted files AND the key file .firm-key.seal (Vibe-Portal QUESTIONS P28): every stored file is unreadable without it, so it is bind-mounted under /opt/vibe/data/apps/vibe-files-portal/ where the appliance backup covers it, and disable never deletes it. ROOT-SERVED at files.<domain> in both routing modes (rootServedOnly): the SPA is built with base '/'. NO emergencyPort, on purpose: session cookies are Secure (PORTAL_URL is https), so sign-in cannot work over the plain-HTTP LAN port, and HAProxy would pass a client's own CF-Connecting-IP through to the app's per-address sign-in limits. routing.clientIpHeader makes Caddy set that header itself (TRUST_CF_CONNECTING_IP=true in the env template); routing.logRedact keeps file names and notes (X-Vibe-Name / X-Vibe-Note, older Vibe Files: ?name= / ?note=) out of Caddy's access log (Vibe-Portal P47). EMAIL: the app refuses to start in production without SMTP (sign-in links and codes go by email), so SMTP is per-app here, independent of the appliance-wide Email & SMS provider. Texts are optional (Twilio). FIRST STAFF ACCOUNT: a one-time setup link printed by a command inside the container (firstLogin.note); later staff, portal keys for Vibe Files, firm name, logo and limits are on the app's own staff page.

required.name: TRUST_CF_CONNECTING_IP
required.doc: Count sign-in limits by CF-Connecting-IP. Safe only because Caddy sets that header itself on this app's vhost (routing.clientIpHeader) and the app has no emergency port.

required.name: EMAIL_PROVIDER
required.doc: The app accepts only smtp in production.

optional.name: VIBE_APP_SUBDOMAIN
optional.doc: Operator override for this app's subdomain label. Empty = the manifest default (files). Consumed by the appliance routing (Caddy vhost + Cloudflare Tunnel CNAME/ingress). Single DNS label — lowercase letters, digits, dashes, no dots.

ui.label: Subdomain
ui.helpText: The <subdomain> in <subdomain>.<your-domain> clients use for the portal. Clients see it in every email, so pick something they will trust. Leave blank for 'files'. Lowercase letters, digits, and dashes; no dots. Saving re-renders routing and re-provisions the Cloudflare Tunnel; the portal briefly restarts.

optional.name: SMTP_HOST
optional.doc: SMTP server hostname. REQUIRED: the portal will not start without it, because client and staff sign-in links and codes go by email.

ui.label: SMTP host
ui.helpText: Required — the portal does not start without email. Hostname only, e.g. smtp.office365.com. The mailbox must be allowed to send by SMTP (Office 365: SMTP AUTH on for that user).

optional.name: SMTP_PORT
optional.doc: SMTP port. 587 (STARTTLS) is typical; 465 for TLS from the start.

ui.label: SMTP port
ui.helpText: 587 for STARTTLS (most providers), 465 for TLS from the start.

ui.label: SMTP username
ui.helpText: Usually the sending mailbox, e.g. portal@yourfirm.com. Leave blank for an unauthenticated relay.

ui.label: SMTP password
ui.helpText: The mailbox password or an app password. Stored in the per-app env file (mode 600). A wrong password shows in the portal's container log at start.

optional.name: SMTP_SECURE
optional.doc: true = TLS from the first byte. Blank = true on port 465, otherwise STARTTLS.

ui.label: TLS from the start
ui.helpText: Leave blank unless your provider says otherwise: port 465 then uses TLS from the start and 587 uses STARTTLS.

optional.name: EMAIL_FROM
optional.doc: From header for the portal's emails. REQUIRED, like SMTP_HOST.

ui.label: From address
ui.helpText: Required. e.g. Your Firm CPA <portal@yourfirm.com> — an address the SMTP mailbox may send as.

optional.name: SMS_PROVIDER
optional.doc: Texts for phone sign-in codes. none = clients sign in by email only.

ui.label: Text messages
ui.helpText: Optional. Twilio lets clients sign in with a code sent to their phone (US/Canada numbers). US numbers need A2P 10DLC registration with Twilio first.

ui.label: Twilio auth token
ui.helpText: Paired with the account SID. Stored in the per-app env file (mode 600).

optional.name: TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER
optional.doc: Sending number in E.164 form (+15551234567). This or TWILIO_MESSAGING_SERVICE_SID.

ui.label: Twilio from number
ui.helpText: e.g. +15551234567. Leave blank if you use a messaging service SID instead.

optional.name: TWILIO_MESSAGING_SERVICE_SID
optional.doc: Twilio messaging service SID (starts with MG). This or TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER.

ui.label: Twilio messaging service SID
ui.helpText: Starts with MG. Leave blank if you set a from number.

firstLogin.note: The portal does not start without email. The FIRST Enable therefore stops with 'SMTP_HOST: required when EMAIL_PROVIDER=smtp' in the container log — expected: fill in SMTP host, port, username, password and From address under Settings → Vibe Portal → Email & SMS, Save, and the portal starts (or set them in /opt/vibe/env/vibe-files-portal.env and Enable again). Then make the first staff account from a one-time link (works once, for 3 days) — copy-paste on the appliance: sudo docker exec vibe-files-portal node_modules/.bin/tsx src/scripts/staff-setup.ts link — open it, set a 12+ character password and add the portal to an authenticator app. More staff, the portal key Vibe Files needs (Settings → Portal keys), the firm name, logo and limits are on the staff page. Locked out: sudo docker exec vibe-files-portal node_modules/.bin/tsx src/scripts/staff-setup.ts reset <email> (add --admin when no admin can sign in). Domain mode only: the portal lives at files.<domain> and has no LAN port. Behind the Cloudflare Tunnel it needs no DNS step; with Let's Encrypt, point files.<domain> at the appliance first.
